author: high5
claim: For the conjugation action of a finite group G of order p^n on itself, every conjugacy class not contained in Z(G) has cardinality divisible by p.
evidence: Let x be outside Z(G). Its stabilizer for conjugation is C_G(x), and orbit-stabilizer gives |Cl_G(x)|=[G:C_G(x)]. By Lagrange, |C_G(x)|=p^m for some 0≤m≤n. Since x is not central, C_G(x) is a proper subgroup, so m<n. Hence |Cl_G(x)|=p^(n-m), which is divisible by p.

links.statement: For the conjugation action of a finite group G of order p^n on itself, every conjugacy class not contained in Z(G) has cardinality divisible by p.

glossary.Cl_G(x): the conjugacy class of x in G
glossary.C_G(x): the centralizer of x in G

author: high5
claim: For a finite group G of order p^n, the class equation implies |G|≡|Z(G)| modulo p.
evidence: The conjugacy classes partition G. The classes of central elements are exactly the singleton classes, so their total contribution is |Z(G)|. Every remaining class has size divisible by p, since its size is the index of a proper centralizer in the p-group G. Thus |G|-|Z(G)| is a sum of multiples of p.

links.statement: For a finite group G of order p^n, the class equation implies |G|≡|Z(G)| modulo p.

author: high
claim: For the conjugation action of G on itself, the fixed points are exactly Z(G), and every orbit of a noncentral element has cardinality divisible by p.
evidence: The orbit of x is Cl_G(x)={gxg^{-1}:g∈G}. The map from left cosets G/C_G(x) to Cl_G(x), gC_G(x)↦gxg^{-1}, is well-defined and bijective, so |Cl_G(x)|=[G:C_G(x)]. By Lagrange's theorem, |C_G(x)| divides |G|=p^n, hence |C_G(x)|=p^m for some 0≤m≤n. If x is noncentral then C_G(x)≠G, so m<n and |Cl_G(x)|=p^{n-m}, a multiple of p. An element is fixed under all conjugations exactly when it commutes with every element of G, i.e. exactly when it lies in Z(G).

links.statement: For the conjugation action of G on itself, the fixed points are exactly Z(G), and every orbit of a noncentral element has cardinality divisible by p.

glossary.C_G(x): the centralizer {g in G : gx=xg} of x in G
glossary.Cl_G(x): the conjugacy class {gxg^{-1} : g in G} of x
glossary.[G:C_G(x)]: the index of C_G(x) in G

author: high
claim: The class equation for the conjugation action gives |G|≡|Z(G)| (mod p); therefore p divides |Z(G)|, and since the identity lies in Z(G), the center has a nonidentity element.
evidence: Choose one representative x_i from each conjugacy class not contained in the center. The partition of G into its central singleton conjugacy classes and its noncentral conjugacy classes gives |G|=|Z(G)|+Σ_i |Cl_G(x_i)|. Every summand in the sum is divisible by p, and |G|=p^n is divisible by p because n≥1. Hence |Z(G)| is divisible by p. Since 1_G∈Z(G), the center is nonempty; its positive cardinality divisible by the prime p is at least p≥2, so it contains an element other than 1_G.

links.statement: The class equation implies p divides |Z(G)| and Z(G) is nontrivial.

glossary.Cl_G(x_i): the conjugacy class of a chosen noncentral representative x_i

author: high3
claim: For the conjugation action of a finite group G of order p^n on itself, every non-singleton orbit has size divisible by p, while the singleton orbits are exactly the elements of Z(G); hence the class equation gives |G| ≡ |Z(G)| (mod p).
evidence: For x in G, the stabilizer under conjugation is C_G(x). The map from left cosets of C_G(x) to the conjugacy class of x, gC_G(x) ↦ gxg^{-1}, is well-defined and bijective, so the orbit has size [G:C_G(x)]. By Lagrange's theorem, |C_G(x)| divides p^n, hence [G:C_G(x)] is a power of p. If x is noncentral then the orbit is not a singleton, so its size is a positive power of p and is divisible by p. The conjugation orbits partition G, and singleton orbits are precisely central elements. Summing orbit sizes therefore yields |G|=|Z(G)| plus a sum of multiples of p; since p divides |G|, p divides |Z(G)|.

links.statement: For the conjugation action, |G| is congruent to |Z(G)| modulo p.

glossary.G: the finite group in the theorem
glossary.C_G(x): the centralizer {g in G : gx=xg} of x in G
glossary.[G:C_G(x)]: the number of left cosets of C_G(x) in G

author: high4
claim: For the conjugation action of G on itself, the fixed points are exactly Z(G), and every nonsingleton orbit has cardinality divisible by p; consequently |G| is congruent to |Z(G)| modulo p.
evidence: An element x is fixed by conjugation by every g in G exactly when gxg^{-1}=x for every g, equivalently when x commutes with every g, so the fixed-point set is Z(G). The orbit of x is in bijection with the left cosets of C_G(x), so its cardinality is [G:C_G(x)]. Because C_G(x) is a subgroup of the finite p-group G, this index divides |G|=p^n and is therefore a power of p. If the orbit is nonsingleton, its size exceeds 1 and hence is divisible by p. The orbit partition consists of |Z(G)| singleton orbits and the nonsingleton orbits, so reducing the resulting cardinality identity modulo p gives the congruence.

links.statement: For the conjugation action of G on itself, fixed points equal Z(G), all nonsingleton orbit sizes are divisible by p, and |G|≡|Z(G)| (mod p).

glossary.p: the prime in the problem statement
glossary.G: the finite group in the problem statement
glossary.Z(G): the center of G, consisting of the elements that commute with every element of G
glossary.C_G(x): the centralizer in G of an element x, namely the subgroup of elements of G commuting with x

author: high2
claim: For the conjugation action of a finite group G of order p^n on itself, every orbit not contained in the center Z(G) has cardinality divisible by p.
evidence: For x in G, its stabilizer under conjugation is C_G(x), so orbit-stabilizer gives |Orb(x)|=[G:C_G(x)]. If x is not central, C_G(x) is a proper subgroup. Lagrange gives |C_G(x)| dividing p^n, hence |C_G(x)|=p^m for an integer m with 0<=m<n. Therefore |Orb(x)|=p^(n-m), which is divisible by p.

links.statement: Every noncentral conjugacy class in a finite p-group has size divisible by p.

glossary.p: the prime in the target theorem
glossary.C_G(x): the centralizer of x in G

author: high6
claim: For a finite group G of order p^n, conjugation partitions G into the singleton classes indexed by Z(G) and noncentral conjugacy classes, each of whose cardinalities is divisible by p; consequently |G| is congruent to |Z(G)| modulo p.
evidence: Let x be noncentral and let C_G(x)={g in G: gx=xg}. The map gC_G(x) -> gxg^{-1} is a bijection from the left cosets of C_G(x) to the conjugacy class of x. Since C_G(x) is a proper subgroup of a group of order p^n, its order is p^m for some m<n, and the class size is [G:C_G(x)]=p^{n-m}, divisible by p. Central elements have singleton conjugacy classes, yielding |G|=|Z(G)| plus a sum of multiples of p.

glossary.C_G(x): the centralizer of x in G
glossary.[G:C_G(x)]: the number of left cosets of C_G(x) in G
